anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
gauntlet: gate=brainstorming/human-batch
Spec amendments: 2 need your call - from the spec review; applying as recommended reopens no tasks; no phase change.

1. Share retry policy - move retry policy into one owner. Adapters currently disagree about when to retry.
   Deciding which part of the system owns retries is an architecture choice, so it needs you.
   Example: adapter-local retry limits -> one coordinator retry limit
   Reviewer: changing retry ownership needs a human architecture choice
   Impact: Retries: each adapter sets its own retry policy -> one shared owner sets the retry policy for every adapter
   A) accept - a new retry service owns every retry policy
   B) alt-1 - the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy; adapters keep running the retries
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: B - reusing the existing coordinator keeps one consistent policy without adding a new service

2. Classify blocked execution - classify exit 126 as blocked rather than failed. Operators need to tell a launch problem apart from a report failure.
   This changes a status operators see, so it needs your decision.
   Example: exit 126 = failed -> blocked
   Reviewer: operator-visible status changes need a human decision
   Impact: Run status: a run that exits with 126 counts as failed -> it counts as blocked
   A) accept - exit 126 is reported as blocked
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: A - a separate status makes launch failures easy to identify

Reply with one line per item: `1. A`, `2. <your own text>`. Bare `1` takes every recommendation.
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" - every later spec amendment in this flow (corrected facts, paths, verification lines, and scope, acceptance-criteria, or public-contract edits alike) applies without asking; only a redraw (changed problem statement, component added, removed, or re-bounded) still stops for you, and the grant never stands in for a spec approval.

Details
crosscut: Design / retries - old: each report adapter owns its retry policy -> new: a new retry service owns all retry policies
crosscut (alt-1): Design / retries - old: each report adapter owns its retry policy -> new: the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy; adapters keep execution
exit126: Design / run status - old: exit 126 is failed -> new: exit 126 is blocked

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved between Before and After: both outputs open each numbered item with the same plain-words what/why sentence, keep A) accept and B) alt-1 with one-line consequences on crosscut, give Recommended: B - and Recommended: A - with reasons, use the `1. A` / `2. <your own text>` reply grammar with bare `1` for all recommendations and no legacy `handle=choice` prompt, and each item still carries exactly one human-call sentence (After's are shorter but still name the architecture choice and the operator-visible status as the reason it needs the human). The only visible differences are cosmetic: After drops the 'Design /' prefix in the Impact lines and splits the crosscut alt-1 into its own Details row, neither of which any fact keys on. If you want to be safe on f6 under rewording, keep the explicit tie to the reviewer ('the reviewer left this to you') as Before did, since the fact permits either the prefilter rule or the escalation reason in plain words and that phrasing anchors both; otherwise the After wording delivers the Change without cost here.
